basics-and-environments.r: A script ran fine on one laptop and failed on another because of different library versions. A virtual environment with a pinned requirements file made the setup the same everywhere.
basics-and-environments.x: Reproducibility is the foundation. Pin direct and transitive dependencies, record the Python version, isolate environments per project and rebuild them from scratch regularly to catch drift.

files-and-processes.r: A script wrote results to a file and crashed halfway, leaving a partial file that a later job treated as complete. Writing to a temporary name and renaming at the end, plus explicit error handling, fixed it.
files-and-processes.x: Treat every external call as failing: files, processes and networks. Use timeouts, check return codes, avoid shell=True with untrusted input and log enough to reconstruct what happened.

http-apis-and-json.r: A job called an API without a timeout, and when the service hung, the job hung forever and blocked the queue. Adding a timeout and a limited retry with backoff made it fail fast and recover.
http-apis-and-json.x: Every request needs a timeout, bounded retries with jitter, idempotency thought and rate-limit respect. Validate responses instead of trusting their shape, and never log tokens.

cloud-sdks.r: A script held a long-lived access key in its source, which later appeared in a screenshot. Using the platform's role-based credentials meant there was no key to leak.
cloud-sdks.x: Prefer identity from the environment over stored keys, handle pagination and throttling, and design operations to be safe on retry. Be careful with scripts that can delete resources: dry-run first.

testing-and-packaging.r: A small command-line tool grew popular inside the company, then broke when a dependency changed. Tests with mocks for the network and a lock file let the team update with confidence.
testing-and-packaging.x: Tests are what let you change code safely. Test behaviour at the edges, keep side effects behind small interfaces, and package tools so installation is a single repeatable command.

concurrency-for-operations.r: A script checked two hundred servers one after another and took an hour. Using a thread pool with a limit of twenty and a per-host timeout finished in three minutes without overwhelming the network.
concurrency-for-operations.x: Concurrency multiplies both speed and blast radius. Cap parallelism, set timeouts, collect errors instead of stopping silently, and choose threads, processes or async based on whether the work waits on I/O or uses CPU.

writing-command-line-tools.r: An internal tool returned exit code 0 even when it failed, so the pipeline kept going on bad data. Returning meaningful exit codes and clear messages made the pipeline stop where it should.
writing-command-line-tools.x: A command-line tool is an API for humans and scripts. Keep output stable, offer machine-readable formats, document exit codes and never change behaviour without a version bump.

logging-for-scripts-and-services.r: A job failed overnight and the only output was a print saying 'done'. After switching to structured logging with levels and context, the next failure showed the exact input and step.
logging-for-scripts-and-services.x: Logs are for the future reader at the worst moment. Log decisions and identifiers, not secrets, use levels sensibly, and make sure logs are shipped and searchable.

yaml-csv-and-config-files.r: A YAML value written as no was read as a boolean, and a setting silently flipped. Quoting values and validating against a schema caught the problem before deploy.
yaml-csv-and-config-files.x: Config formats have traps: type coercion, anchors, encoding and delimiters. Validate against a schema, load with safe loaders only and treat configuration changes as code changes.

debugging-python.r: A script seemed to hang. Sending it a signal to dump the stack showed it waiting on a network call without a timeout, which was the actual cause. The fix was a two-line timeout, found in minutes because the stack showed where it waited.
debugging-python.x: Read tracebacks from the bottom, reproduce with the smallest input, and use the debugger or tracing for state you cannot guess. For long-running services, build in the ability to inspect them safely in production.

sre-automation-aws-with-boto3-safely.r: A cleanup script found no unattached volumes in the test account and then deleted fourteen in production. It had used the default region, an admin role and no dry run. Snapshots restored the data, and the tool now prints a plan and requires --apply.
sre-automation-aws-with-boto3-safely.x: Automation should have its own least-privilege role and leave an audit trail. A missing tag means ask the owner, not delete. The cost of one wrong region or one missed page is far higher than the time saved.

sre-automation-kubernetes-client-scripts.r: A daily report said no pod restarted more than five times, yet a checkout service crash-looped all week. Each replacement pod started at zero. Grouping by owner and counting pods created per day exposed the loop immediately.
sre-automation-kubernetes-client-scripts.x: Report at the level where the problem lives. Counting restarts per pod missed a crash loop because the controller kept creating new pods, so group by workload and check readiness too.

sre-automation-retries-backoff-timeouts-.r: A database failover lasted twenty seconds, but thousands of clients retried with no delay and no limit. The new primary was flooded as soon as it started and fell over again. Backoff with jitter and retry budgets stopped the next failover from escalating.
sre-automation-retries-backoff-timeouts-.x: A timeout does not mean a request failed. Retries are safe only when the operation is repeatable. Unbounded immediate retries turn a short failover into a long outage.

sre-automation-parsing-logs-and-building.r: A draft post-mortem said errors began before the deploy and nearly cleared the release. The load balancer logged local time without an offset. After converting to UTC the first error came thirty seconds after the deploy, which pointed to the real cause.
sre-automation-parsing-logs-and-building.x: Time zone mistakes produce wrong stories. Generate the timeline from data instead of copying times by hand, and keep the script so the next review is faster and more consistent.

sre-automation-chatops-alert-handlers-an.r: During a real outage the key alert was missed because a flapping node alert had posted 312 times in the channel. Fingerprint grouping with a cooldown and routing by severity kept the next incident channel short and readable.
sre-automation-chatops-alert-handlers-an.x: Never turn chat text into a shell command. Keep actions on an allow list, make them idempotent and time-limited, and route alerts so the one that matters is not buried under noise.

sre-automation-safe-bulk-operations-and-.r: A script updated an agent setting on 600 of 800 hosts in four minutes using 50 workers, and the value was wrong. With no canary, health gate or kill switch, recovery meant writing a rollback during the incident. The rebuilt tool batches, checks health and stops on request.
sre-automation-safe-bulk-operations-and-.x: Bulk tools multiply mistakes. Safety features such as plan files, batch sizes, health gates and kill switches are part of the tool, not extras, and they are cheap compared with a fleet-wide incident.
